title: Super-resolution & Reconstruction
interviewAnswer: Super-resolution infers a higher-resolution signal from limited observations. The central tension is recovering detail without hallucinating unsupported structure, so downstream/domain validation is often essential.
why: Super-resolution/reconstruction interviews test whether you distinguish resolution enhancement, hallucination risk, paired/unpaired data and task-specific validation.
intuition: The model maps a low-information input to a higher-resolution output. Because multiple high-resolution images can correspond to one low-resolution input, the problem is inherently ambiguous.
deepDive: Classical interpolation is deterministic and smooth but cannot invent missing high-frequency content. Supervised SR learns from aligned LR/HR pairs with pixel/perceptual/adversarial losses. Generative SR can create realistic texture but may hallucinate details. Scientific reconstruction therefore needs downstream structural/physical validation. 3D SR adds volumetric consistency and heavy compute constraints.
workedExample: A GAN can make SEM-like texture visually sharp while altering pore boundaries; PSNR/perceptual metrics alone cannot prove porosity correctness.
commonMistakes: Equating visually sharp output with ground-truth recovery.
Ignoring whether LR/HR pairs are aligned.
followUps: Why can GAN SR lower PSNR?
How do you validate scientific SR?
production: Choose output acceptance metrics tied to downstream use, version preprocessing/scale factors, and use batch/GPU jobs for large 3D outputs.
